headline: In Barcelona, Russian and Ukrainian exiles cross paths at the baths: 'We don't talk about the war, not even at the banya'
subhead: For the past year, traditional steam baths from Eastern Europe and Russia have been springing up across the Catalan capital. Popular with both Russians and Ukrainians – who arrived by the thousands on the Costa Brava at the start of the war in 2022 – the establishments have become an unexpected place for the two communities to coexist.

headline: 'Bolle Jos,' the Dutch cocaine baron who became Sierra Leone's viceroy
subhead: 'Africa under the influence' (5/6). Sentenced in the Netherlands to seven years in prison for importing 11 metric tons of cocaine, Jos Leijdekkers, the son-in-law of Sierra Leone's president, has continued to run his drug operations with impunity from Freetown.

headline: In Nantes, La Cigale is an Art Nouveau restaurant that nearly runs itself
subhead: 'More Than Just A Restaurant' (6/6). In this emblematic Art Nouveau establishment, listed as a historic monument, owner Yannick Curty prefers to step back, insisting the staff can manage without him. And it seems to be working.

headline: Cape Verde offers fragile refuge for many persecuted African homosexuals: 'It's like I'm a prisoner in paradise'
subhead: The most LGBTQ+ tolerant country in Africa, according to a survey by Afrobarometer, the archipelago has become home to many Africans fleeing repression tied to their sexual orientation. However, the lack of an asylum policy has prevented them from obtaining residency permits.
